cells.remarks: Registers that Arasāḷuḍaiyān Irayiyavan Paḷḷavayan alias Mammudi-gōḷa Pōsan, the supervisor of the temple of Tiruttikkali-Ālvar at Tikkali-Vaḷḷam, in Mīyāṭu-nāḍu, a sub-division of Paḍuvūr-kōṭṭam, finding that one of the directors (gaṇattar) of the village had received 25 poṇ, weighed by the standard weight Dharmakaṭṭalai-tuḷai-nira-poṇ, and kept a perpetual lamp founded by Śiṅgapirāṭiyār and the his nephew-in-law (son-in-law) (marumagan) Sarvadichōḍaṅgavi had neglected to maintain the lamp, now made a gift of 600 kuḷi of his land for continuing the charity.

cells.date: Saka 1349, Plavanga, Jihanus, su. dasami, Monday, Karttika.
cells.remarks: States that in pursuance of the royal order communicated to the Siva and Vishnu temples of Kanchipuram, Tirukkalatti, Tiruvallam, Tiruvallangadu and Tiruppalaivanam the tax-free villages in the various districts of Chandragiri-rajya and in conformity with the orders of the Dandanayaka Bhikshavritti Aiyagal and Devaraya-Udaiyar of Chandragiri, the Mahesvaras and Vayirava-Nayanar obtained an order to the effect that all the taxes and obligations except vibhuti-kanikkai which were due to the king from the temple of Tiruvul-udaiya-Nayanar must be deposited in the temple treasury and that out of this fund, worship, repairs and festivals be to be conducted in the temple by them.

cells.remarks: Records that Śūrappa-Nāyaka, son of Poṭṭappa-Nāyaka, who bears the title 'Māṇigamuravarādichēvara', and who belonged to the Kāḍyapa gōtra, made a gift of wet and dry lands for offerings and festivals to the god Āḷvargal-Nāyiṉār at the southern bank of the Peṇṇai in Tiruvāḍi-śīrmai, a subdivision of Tirumuṇaippāḍi-vaḷanāḍu, which was itself a portion of Vaḷudilampaṭṭu-śāvadi (i.e. ēhavadi) in Kurukkai-kūṛṛam, a district of Maḷāḍu alias Jānanātha-vaḷanāḍu. It is also recorded that a number of lands as above which had already been gifted to the temple and had been resigned are lying uncultivated and that they were now made tax-free by Emberumān-Jiyar. Services named Aliya-Rāmarāyar, Śūrappa-Nāyaka and Kṛishṇama-Nāyakar are also referred to. Tirukkoilūr is called the sacred place of the first three Āḷvār (mudal-āḷvār).

cells.remarks: Records that as the taxes Inavari and Iḍaṅgai-vari collected from the Valangai and Iḍaṅgai communities were exorbitant and the villagers were distressed and migrated to other places and the country became depopulated, the king had sent an order to Nāgarasa-Uḍaiyār authorising him to cancel these taxes, and as Aṇṇappa-Uḍaiyār to whom this was communicated failed for execution engraved it only at certain odd places, a further petition was preferred to Nāgarasa-Uḍaiyār and this order was then caused to be engraved at Tiruveṇṇainallūr.

cells.remarks: States that, as the village of Tiruvamattūr was lying deserted for a long time, the temple maṇḍapas and gōpuras were ruined and the irrigation tank had breached, the king made a gift of certain taxes and ordered that this amount, the necessary repairs should be carried out and worship conducted in the temple, in the name of Narasiṅgarāja-Udaiyar. The order was issued by Avasaram Aṇṇamann-ēar, agent of the king, to the trustees of the temple who managed the temple lands.

cells.place: On a slab built in the revetment of the irrigation tank at Teņnerī neer the sixth mile-stone on the road from Walajabad.
cells.remarks: States that when the tank at Teņnerī had breached owing to heavy rains in the month of Margali, of the year Sarvari and no one was able to offer any closure, Eluttur Immadi Kumara-Tachārya repaired the tank with the grace of the goddess Lakshmi, renamed it as Tatusamudram and attained great fame.

cells.place: On a slab set up in a forest near Dodra, Nowrangpur taluk, Jeypore State, Vizagapatam agency.
cells.remarks: Mutilated and damaged. Describes the heroism and good qualities of a certain Gōpāladēva who defeated the chiefs of Gōkarṇa, Karṇāṭa, etc., and attained to the position of a rāṇaka. Registers the gift of the two villages Pippalapuṇḍi and Koṇavu as garuḍakēbha by Maṇḍalapati to Paṇḍitāchārya Rāṇaka Śrī Vāvanadēva. The grant was renewed later by the princesses Sugaladēvi, the daughter of Sahadēva and Pāmpādēvi the daughter of Rāṇaka Śrī Vāvanadēva, the lord of Ālakoṇḍa, and by their sons. Among the witnesses figure the queen Vīrabhāmāhadēvi.

cells.remarks: Damaged. Begins with a praise of God Hari. The king Bhavadatta is said to have belonged to the race of Nala. Registers the installation of god Hari at the foot of Poḍa and the foundation of a satra (feeding house) for Brāhmaṇas and Yatis (ascetics) and the provision made in the shape of bhūri-dakshiṇā. Records the names of Rāṇaka Kīrttirāja and his brother Rāṇaka Śindara.
